title: Boolean valuation of atoms
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tape alphabet, let $\mathrm{Ans}$ assign a Boolean value to each selector and pair of natural numbers, and let $W,n,t,a,j\in\mathbb{N}$ and $xb\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Define the Boolean value of each atom as follows: an answer atom is evaluated by applying $\mathrm{Ans}$ to its selector with the encoded time and address; the length atom is true; the time and address not-at-their-maximum atoms assert respectively $t+1<2^W$ and $a+1<2^W$; the zero and index atoms assert respectively $a=0$, $j=0$, $j<n$, $j\le n$, and $j=n+1$; and the input-bit atom has value $xb$.
hypotheses_covered: answer function on selectors and pairs of natural numbers
